text:
emily: heads-up - the new edge quickstart is tripping TS inference at the edge build step. Our helper's generic collapses to `any` for consumers after SWC+rollup. Not seen in local node dev.

derek: can you paste the minimal snippet and tsconfig? first thought: resolver picks up wrong .d.ts (cjs vs esm) or the impl signature leaked into the published declarations.

emily: minimal repro below. works fine with `tsc --noEmit` in node, but when packaging for the edge with swc/rollup the consumer types become `any`.

```ts
// packages/sdk/src/pipe.ts
export type PipeOpts<T = unknown> = { meta?: T }
export function pipeThrough<T>(opts: PipeOpts<T>): { run: () => T }
export function pipeThrough(opts: PipeOpts<any>) { return { run: () => (opts.meta as any) } }

// app/main.ts
const p = pipeThrough({ meta: { session: 'abc' } })
// expect p.run() -> { session: string } but edge bundle shows `any`
```

emily: example tsconfig in the repo: 
```json
{ "compilerOptions": { "module": "ESNext", "moduleResolution": "bundler", "target": "ES2020", "strict": true } }
```

priya: that smells like an impl-signature leak. Also check package.json `exports` map - if `types` points to a single d.ts path but bundler resolves imports differently, TS might resolve a d.ts that includes the implementation signature. Do we publish dual d.ts files?

derek: we do: we ship dist/esm, dist/cjs and one dist/types built from source. Strange thing: rollup + swc can rewrite imports causing TS to not follow the same resolution order as node. I bet `moduleResolution: bundler` + our conditional exports confuses it.

toni: two approaches: 1) change d.ts emit so public API surface only has `declare` overloads, 2) refactor API to avoid relying on cross-package inference (e.g., return a typed wrapper type WithMeta<T>). Option 1 is non-breaking.

priya: for 1) we can mark the implementation with /** @internal */ and enable `stripInternal` in declaration build. That will remove the `opts: PipeOpts<any>` impl signature from published d.ts. Also prefer `unknown` over `any` in public types to avoid accidental widening.

derek: short-term mitigation for examples: update example tsconfig to `moduleResolution: node16` and add an onboarding note. Longer term: add a typing smoke test in examples CI that runs `tsc --noEmit` with both `moduleResolution: bundler` and `node16`.

emily: created issue DX-4745: "edge bundle widens generic overload to any in examples" and attached the repro. (assign: @derek).

build-bot: DX-4745 created and linked: https://tracker/redwood/DX-4745 (assignee: derek).

derek: plan-of-action:
- add a tiny typing check in packages/sdk/typing-tests/edge-pipe.ts that asserts inference for ESM bundles
- change declaration emit to only expose `declare` overloads and mark impl internal
- update examples tsconfig and README as temporary stopgap
- add CI job in examples that runs `tsc --noEmit` with both moduleResolution settings

toni: one more defensive idea: ship a small helper `unwrapMeta<T>(x: PipeOpts<T>): T` so consumers can explicitly assert the generic. That avoids relying on type inference across package boundaries, but it's an extra step for users. Could mention it in migration docs.

emily: fine with the helper as a docs fallback. holding the quickstart PR until the typings fix lands so we don't ship a broken starter.

derek: will open PR with d.ts changes and CI test tomorrow, ping here when ready.

build-bot: PR #1378 -> DX-4745 (open).

emily: saw PR, thanks! will test against vercel edge sample once merged.
